extractions.quote: We report the case of a female patient, who died at the age of 66 years. Besides an insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus (IDDM) she had developed the clinical symptoms of stiff-man-syndrome (SMS) and harbored autoantibodies against glutamate-decarboxylase (GAD) in blood and liquor.

In the further course of the disease, muscle convulsions in proximal extremities and shoulders increased.

During the clinical evaluation the following observations were made: strong lumbal lordosis and opisthotonus (especially following external triggers and psychic tension), later a rigor-like increase of skeletal muscle tonus in the extremities, strong reflexes, no pathological reflexes, vegetative crises including tachypnoia, flashes.

extractions.value: clinical features (stiffness, spasms, hyperlordosis, opisthotonus); GAD antibodies in blood and CSF; EMG showing loss of interneurons; response to clonazepam; exclusion of tumor by autopsy
extractions.quote: During the clinical evaluation the following observations were made: strong lumbal lordosis and opisthotonus (especially following external triggers and psychic tension), later a rigor-like increase of skeletal muscle tonus in the extremities, strong reflexes, no pathological reflexes, vegetative crises including tachypnoia, flashes. Standard laboratory tests: GAD antibodies were detected in blood (7,000 U/ml) and liquor cerebrospinalis (not quantified), negative results of tetanus test (on animals), and microbiological tests for clostridium species. EMG revealed hints for a loss of interneurons in the spinal cord. As described in literature, the clinical symptoms decayed following clonazepam administration. During clinical and pathological examinations no hints for a tumor were found.
